clinicalPearls: Recurrent passage of loose or watery stools without predominant abdominal pain or bloating
The absence of significant pain distinguishes it from diarrhoea-predominant irritable bowel syndrome
It is a diagnosis made after excluding organic causes of chronic diarrhoea
Important mimics include coeliac disease, microscopic colitis, bile acid diarrhoea and inflammatory bowel disease
Nocturnal diarrhoea, weight loss or bleeding are not typical and should prompt investigation
Management includes dietary review and antidiarrhoeal or bile-acid-binding therapy where appropriate
reference.pathophysiology: Functional diarrhoea is a disorder of gut-brain interaction characterised by accelerated colonic transit and altered secretion and motility without a structural or biochemical cause. Visceral hypersensitivity and disturbed gut-brain signalling contribute, and there is overlap with diarrhoea-predominant irritable bowel syndrome, from which it is separated chiefly by the lack of prominent pain. Because several organic conditions can produce an identical clinical picture, the diagnosis depends on their reasonable exclusion.
additionalInvestigations: Coeliac serology and, where indicated, faecal calprotectin
Assessment for bile acid diarrhoea in suitable patients
Colonoscopy with biopsies to exclude microscopic colitis where appropriate
Blood tests for inflammatory, thyroid and malabsorptive causes
Stool studies where infection or malabsorption is suspected
reference.prognosis: The condition is benign and often fluctuates over time; symptoms are usually controllable with dietary measures and targeted antidiarrhoeal treatment.
pitfalls: Missing microscopic colitis, which needs biopsies to diagnose
Overlooking bile acid diarrhoea as a treatable cause
Attributing organic diarrhoea to a functional cause
references: Sleisenger and Fordtran's Gastrointestinal and Liver Disease
